cards.back: Ramapithecus was more man-like while Dryopithecus was more ape-like.
cards.quote: Ramapithecus was more man-like while Dryopithecus was more ape-like.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Where were fossils of man-like bones discovered?
cards.back: Few fossils of man-like bones have been discovered in Ethiopia and Tanzania
cards.quote: Few fossils of man-like bones have been discovered in Ethiopia and Tanzania

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What did hominid fossils suggest about man-like primates 3-4 mya?
cards.back: These revealed hominid features leading to the belief that about 3-4 mya, man-like primates walked in eastern Africa.
cards.quote: These revealed hominid features leading to the belief that about 3-4 mya, man-like primates walked in eastern Africa.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who probably lived in the East African grasslands two mya?
cards.back: Two mya, Australopithecines probably lived in East African grasslands.
cards.quote: Two mya, Australopithecines probably lived in East African grasslands.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What did Australopithecines hunt with and essentially eat?
cards.back: Evidence shows they hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit.
cards.quote: Evidence shows they hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which creature was called the first human-like being, the hominid?
cards.back: This creature was called the first human-like being the hominid and was called Homo habilis.
cards.quote: This creature was called the first human-like being the hominid and was called Homo habilis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What was the brain capacity of Homo habilis?
cards.back: The brain capacities were between 650-800cc.
cards.quote: The brain capacities were between 650-800cc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed which stage of human evolution?
cards.back: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed the next stage, i.e., Homo erectus about 1.5 mya.
cards.quote: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed the next stage, i.e., Homo erectus about 1.5 mya.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What was the brain size of Homo erectus?
cards.back: Homo erectus had a large brain around 900cc.
cards.quote: Homo erectus had a large brain around 900cc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What did Homo erectus probably eat?
cards.back: Homo erectus probably ate meat.
cards.quote: Homo erectus probably ate meat.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which man had a brain size of 1400cc and lived in near east and central Asia?
cards.back: The Neanderthal man with a brain size of 1400cc lived in near east and central Asia between 1,00,000-40,000 years back.
cards.quote: The Neanderthal man with a brain size of 1400cc lived in near east and central Asia between 1,00,000-40,000 years back.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What did Neanderthal man use hides for, and what did he do for his dead?
cards.back: They used hides to protect their body and buried their dead.
cards.quote: They used hides to protect their body and buried their dead.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Where did Homo sapiens arise?
cards.back: Homo sapiens arose in Africa and moved across continents and developed into distinct races.
cards.quote: Homo sapiens arose in Africa and moved across continents and developed into distinct races.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: When did modern Homo sapiens arise?
cards.back: During ice age between 75,000-10,000 years ago modern Homo sapiens arose.
cards.quote: During ice age between 75,000-10,000 years ago modern Homo sapiens arose.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: When did agriculture arise and human settlements start?
cards.back: Agriculture came around 10,000 years back and human settlements started.
cards.quote: Agriculture came around 10,000 years back and human settlements started.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Most scientists believe ____, i.e., formation of biomolecules preceded the appearance of the first cellular forms of life.
cards.back: Most scientists believe chemical evolution, i.e., formation of biomolecules preceded the appearance of the first cellular forms of life.
cards.quote: Most scientists believe chemical evolution, i.e., formation of biomolecules preceded the appearance of the first cellular forms of life.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Homology is accounted for by the idea of ____.
cards.back: Homology is accounted for by the idea of branching descent.
cards.quote: Homology is accounted for by the idea of branching descent.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which studies provide evidence for evolution?
cards.back: Study of comparative anatomy, fossils and comparative biochemistry provides evidence for evolution.
cards.quote: Study of comparative anatomy, fossils and comparative biochemistry provides evidence for evolution.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define health.
cards.back: It could be defined as a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being.
cards.quote: It could be defined as a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the three things that affect health.
cards.back:
genetic disorders
infections
life style including food and water we take, rest and exercise we give to our bodies, habits that we have or lack
cards.quote: (i) genetic disorders — deficiencies with which a child is born and deficiencies/defects which the child inherits from parents from birth; (ii) infections and (iii) life style including food and water we take, rest and exercise we give to our bodies, habits that we have or lack

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which habits are very important to maintain good health?
cards.back: Balanced diet, personal hygiene and regular exercise are very important to maintain good health.
cards.quote: Balanced diet, personal hygiene and regular exercise are very important to maintain good health.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is a disease?
cards.back: When the functioning of one or more organs or systems of the body is adversely affected, characterised by appearance of various signs and symptoms, we say that we are not healthy, i.e., we have a disease.
cards.quote: When the functioning of one or more organs or systems of the body is adversely affected, characterised by appearance of various signs and symptoms, we say that we are not healthy, i.e., we have a disease.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Types of diseases (broad grouping)
cards.back:
infectious
non-infectious
cards.quote: Diseases can be broadly grouped into infectious and non-infectious.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are infectious diseases?
cards.back: Diseases which are easily transmitted from one person to another, are called infectious diseases.
cards.quote: Diseases which are easily transmitted from one person to another, are called infectious diseases.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Among non-infectious diseases, which is the major cause of death?
cards.back: Among non-infectious diseases, cancer is the major cause of death.
cards.quote: Among non-infectious diseases, cancer is the major cause of death.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Groups of organisms that cause diseases in man
cards.back:
bacteria
viruses
fungi
protozoans
helminths
cards.quote: A wide range of organisms belonging to bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, helminths, etc., could cause diseases in man.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are disease-causing organisms called?
cards.back: Such disease-causing organisms are called pathogens.
cards.quote: Such disease-causing organisms are called pathogens.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ is a pathogenic bacterium which causes typhoid fever in human beings.
cards.back: Salmonella typhi is a pathogenic bacterium which causes typhoid fever in human beings.
cards.quote: Salmonella typhi is a pathogenic bacterium which causes typhoid fever in human beings.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How do typhoid pathogens enter the body and spread to other organs?
cards.back: These pathogens generally enter the small intestine through food and water contaminated with them and migrate to other organs through blood.
cards.quote: These pathogens generally enter the small intestine through food and water contaminated with them and migrate to other organs through blood.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Typhoid: what temperature does the sustained high fever reach?
cards.back: Sustained high fever (39° to 40°C), weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache and loss of appetite are some of the common symptoms of this disease.
cards.quote: Sustained high fever (39° to 40°C), weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache and loss of appetite are some of the common symptoms of this disease.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which test confirms typhoid fever?
cards.back: Typhoid fever could be confirmed by Widal test.
cards.quote: Typhoid fever could be confirmed by Widal test.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which bacteria are responsible for pneumonia in humans?
cards.back: Bacteria like Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae are responsible for the disease pneumonia in humans which infects the alveoli (air filled sacs) of the lungs.
cards.quote: Bacteria like Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae are responsible for the disease pneumonia in humans which infects the alveoli (air filled sacs) of the lungs.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Pneumonia: what happens in the alveoli, causing respiratory problems?
cards.back: As a result of the infection, the alveoli get filled with fluid leading to severe problems in respiration.
cards.quote: As a result of the infection, the alveoli get filled with fluid leading to severe problems in respiration.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How does a healthy person acquire pneumonia?
cards.back: A healthy person acquires the infection by inhaling the droplets/aerosols released by an infected person or even by sharing glasses and utensils with an infected person.
cards.quote: A healthy person acquires the infection by inhaling the droplets/aerosols released by an infected person or even by sharing glasses and utensils with an infected person.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ represent one such group of viruses which cause one of the most infectious human ailments — the common cold.
cards.back: Rhino viruses represent one such group of viruses which cause one of the most infectious human ailments — the common cold.
cards.quote: Rhino viruses represent one such group of viruses which cause one of the most infectious human ailments — the common cold.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which parts does the common cold infect, and which part does it not?
cards.back: They infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs.
cards.quote: They infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Common cold: for how many days do the symptoms usually last?
cards.back: The common cold is characterised by nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache, tiredness, etc., which usually last for 3-7 days.
cards.quote: The common cold is characterised by nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache, tiredness, etc., which usually last for 3-7 days.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How is the common cold transmitted to a healthy person?
cards.back: Droplets resulting from cough or sneezes of an infected person are either inhaled directly or transmitted through contaminated objects such as pens, books, cups, doorknobs, computer keyboard or mouse, etc., and cause infection in a healthy person.
cards.quote: Droplets resulting from cough or sneezes of an infected person are either inhaled directly or transmitted through contaminated objects such as pens, books, cups, doorknobs, computer keyboard or mouse, etc., and cause infection in a healthy person.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which protozoan causes malaria?
cards.back: Plasmodium, a tiny protozoan is responsible for this disease.
cards.quote: Plasmodium, a tiny protozoan is responsible for this disease.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Species of Plasmodium causing different types of malaria
cards.back:
P. vivax
P. malaria
P. falciparum
cards.quote: Different species of Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. malaria and P. falciparum) are responsible for different types of malaria.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which type of malaria is the most serious and can even be fatal?
cards.back: Of these, malignant malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum is the most serious one and can even be fatal.
cards.quote: Of these, malignant malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum is the most serious one and can even be fatal.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In what form, and through the bite of which mosquito, does Plasmodium enter the human body?
cards.back: Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito.
cards.quote: Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Plasmodium in the human body: where does it first multiply, and what does it attack next?
cards.back: The parasites initially multiply within the liver cells and then attack the red blood cells (RBCs) resulting in their rupture.
cards.quote: The parasites initially multiply within the liver cells and then attack the red blood cells (RBCs) resulting in their rupture.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which toxic substance released on RBC rupture causes the recurring chill and high fever in malaria?
cards.back: The rupture of RBCs is associated with release of a toxic substance, haemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever recurring every three to four days.
cards.quote: The rupture of RBCs is associated with release of a toxic substance, haemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever recurring every three to four days.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Where are sporozoites formed and stored in the female Anopheles mosquito?
cards.back: The parasites multiply within them to form sporozoites that are stored in their salivary glands.
cards.quote: The parasites multiply within them to form sporozoites that are stored in their salivary glands.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many hosts does the malarial parasite need, and which one is the vector?
cards.back: It is interesting to note that the malarial parasite requires two hosts — human and mosquitoes — to complete its life cycle (Figure 7.1); the female Anopheles mosquito is the vector (transmitting agent) too.
cards.quote: It is interesting to note that the malarial parasite requires two hosts — human and mosquitoes — to complete its life cycle (Figure 7.1); the female Anopheles mosquito is the vector (transmitting agent) too.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ is a protozoan parasite in the large intestine of human which causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery).
cards.back: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite in the large intestine of human which causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery).
cards.quote: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite in the large intestine of human which causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Amoebiasis: name its symptoms.
cards.back: Symptoms of this disease include constipation, abdominal pain and cramps, stools with excess mucous and blood clots.
cards.quote: Symptoms of this disease include constipation, abdominal pain and cramps, stools with excess mucous and blood clots.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What role do houseflies play in amoebiasis?
cards.back: Houseflies act as mechanical carriers and serve to transmit the parasite from faeces of infected person to food and food products, thereby contaminating them.
cards.quote: Houseflies act as mechanical carriers and serve to transmit the parasite from faeces of infected person to food and food products, thereby contaminating them.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Amoebiasis: what is the main source of infection?
cards.back: Drinking water and food contaminated by the faecal matter are the main source of infection.
cards.quote: Drinking water and food contaminated by the faecal matter are the main source of infection.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Ascaris, the common round worm and Wuchereria, the filarial worm, are some of the ____ which are known to be pathogenic to man.
cards.back: Ascaris, the common round worm and Wuchereria, the filarial worm, are some of the helminths which are known to be pathogenic to man.
cards.quote: Ascaris, the common round worm and Wuchereria, the filarial worm, are some of the helminths which are known to be pathogenic to man.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Ascariasis: name its symptoms.
cards.back: Symptoms of these disease include internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anemia and blockage of the intestinal passage.
cards.quote: Symptoms of these disease include internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anemia and blockage of the intestinal passage.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How is ascariasis spread through eggs of the parasite?
cards.back: The eggs of the parasite are excreted along with the faeces of infected persons which contaminate soil, water, plants, etc. A healthy person acquires this infection through contaminated water, vegetables, fruits, etc.
cards.quote: The eggs of the parasite are excreted along with the faeces of infected persons which contaminate soil, water, plants, etc. A healthy person acquires this infection through contaminated water, vegetables, fruits, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which worms cause filariasis (elephantiasis), and which organs do they usually affect?
cards.back: Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi), the filarial worms cause a slowly developing chronic inflammation of the organs in which they live for many years, usually the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs and the disease is called elephantiasis or filariasis
cards.quote: Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi), the filarial worms cause a slowly developing chronic inflammation of the organs in which they live for many years, usually the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs and the disease is called elephantiasis or filariasis

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How are filarial pathogens transmitted to a healthy person?
cards.back: The pathogens are transmitted to a healthy person through the bite by the female mosquito vectors.
cards.quote: The pathogens are transmitted to a healthy person through the bite by the female mosquito vectors.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Fungal genera responsible for ringworms
cards.back:
Microsporum
Trichophyton
Epidermophyton
cards.quote: Many fungi belonging to the genera Microsporum, Trichophyton and Epidermophyton are

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Ringworm: what are the main symptoms?
cards.back: Appearance of dry, scaly lesions on various parts of the body such as skin, nails and scalp (Figure 7.3) are the main symptoms of the disease.
cards.quote: Appearance of dry, scaly lesions on various parts of the body such as skin, nails and scalp (Figure 7.3) are the main symptoms of the disease.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which conditions help ringworm fungi grow, and where do they thrive?
cards.back: Heat and moisture help these fungi to grow, which makes them thrive in skin folds such as those in the groin or between the toes.
cards.quote: Heat and moisture help these fungi to grow, which makes them thrive in skin folds such as those in the groin or between the toes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do measures for personal hygiene include?
cards.back: Measures for personal hygiene include keeping the body clean; consumption of clean drinking water, food, vegetables, fruits, etc.
cards.quote: Measures for personal hygiene include keeping the body clean; consumption of clean drinking water, food, vegetables, fruits, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does public hygiene include?
cards.back: Public hygiene includes proper disposal of waste and excreta; periodic cleaning and disinfection of water reservoirs, pools, cesspools and tanks and observing standard practices of hygiene in public catering.
cards.quote: Public hygiene includes proper disposal of waste and excreta; periodic cleaning and disinfection of water reservoirs, pools, cesspools and tanks and observing standard practices of hygiene in public catering.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Malaria and filariasis: what is the most important preventive measure?
cards.back: For diseases such as malaria and filariasis that are transmitted through insect vectors, the most important measure is to control or eliminate the vectors and their breeding places.
cards.quote: For diseases such as malaria and filariasis that are transmitted through insect vectors, the most important measure is to control or eliminate the vectors and their breeding places.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the measures to control mosquitoes and their breeding places.
cards.back:
avoiding stagnation of water in and around residential areas
regular cleaning of household coolers
use of mosquito nets
introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds that feed on mosquito larvae
spraying of insecticides in ditches, drainage areas and swamps
doors and windows should be provided with wire mesh to prevent the entry of mosquitoes
cards.quote: avoiding stagnation of water in and around residential areas, regular cleaning of household coolers, use of mosquito nets, introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds that feed on mosquito larvae, spraying of insecticides in ditches, drainage areas and swamps, etc. In addition, doors and windows should be provided with wire mesh to prevent the entry of mosquitoes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which fish introduced in ponds feeds on mosquito larvae?
cards.back: introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds that feed on mosquito larvae
cards.quote: introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds that feed on mosquito larvae

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Dengue and chikungunya are vector-borne diseases of which mosquitoes?
cards.back: Such precautions have become more important especially in the light of recent widespread incidences of the vector-borne (Aedes mosquitoes) diseases like dengue and chikungunya in many parts of India.
cards.quote: Such precautions have become more important especially in the light of recent widespread incidences of the vector-borne (Aedes mosquitoes) diseases like dengue and chikungunya in many parts of India.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which deadly disease has been completely eradicated by vaccines and immunisation programmes?
cards.back: The use of vaccines and immunisation programmes have enabled us to completely eradicate a deadly disease like smallpox.
cards.quote: The use of vaccines and immunisation programmes have enabled us to completely eradicate a deadly disease like smallpox.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the diseases (other than smallpox) controlled to a large extent by vaccines.
cards.back:
polio
diphtheria
pneumonia
tetanus
cards.quote: A large number of other infectious diseases like polio, diphtheria, pneumonia and tetanus have been controlled to a large extent by the use of vaccines.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define immunity.
cards.back: This overall ability of the host to fight the disease-causing organisms, conferred by the immune system is called immunity.
cards.quote: This overall ability of the host to fight the disease-causing organisms, conferred by the immune system is called immunity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Types of immunity
cards.back:
Innate immunity
Acquired immunity
cards.quote: Immunity is of two types: (i) Innate immunity and (ii) Acquired immunity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is innate immunity?
cards.back: Innate immunity is non-specific type of defence, that is present at the time of birth.
cards.quote: Innate immunity is non-specific type of defence, that is present at the time of birth.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Innate immunity consists of how many types of barriers?
cards.back: Innate immunity consist of four types of barriers.
cards.quote: Innate immunity consist of four types of barriers.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Innate immunity: what are the physical barriers?
cards.back: Skin on our body is the main barrier which prevents entry of the micro-organisms. Mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts also help in trapping microbes entering our body.
cards.quote: Skin on our body is the main barrier which prevents entry of the micro-organisms. Mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts also help in trapping microbes entering our body.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Innate immunity: what are the physiological barriers?
cards.back: Acid in the stomach, saliva in the mouth, tears from eyes—all prevent microbial growth.
cards.quote: Acid in the stomach, saliva in the mouth, tears from eyes—all prevent microbial growth.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Cellular barrier of innate immunity: which blood cells and tissue cells phagocytose and destroy microbes?
cards.back: Certain types of leukocytes (WBC) of our body like polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils) and monocytes and natural killer (type of lymphocytes) in the blood as well as macrophages in tissues can phagocytose and destroy microbes.
cards.quote: Certain types of leukocytes (WBC) of our body like polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils) and monocytes and natural killer (type of lymphocytes) in the blood as well as macrophages in tissues can phagocytose and destroy microbes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called ____ which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.
cards.back: Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.
cards.quote: Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Acquired immunity, on the other hand is pathogen specific. It is characterised by ____.
cards.back: Acquired immunity, on the other hand is pathogen specific. It is characterised by memory.
cards.quote: Acquired immunity, on the other hand is pathogen specific. It is characterised by memory.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Primary vs secondary immune response: the difference on intensity
cards.back: when our body encounters a pathogen for the first time it produces a response called primary response which is of low intensity. Subsequent encounter with the same pathogen elicits a highly intensified secondary or anamnestic response.
cards.quote: when our body encounters a pathogen for the first time it produces a response called primary response which is of low intensity. Subsequent encounter with the same pathogen elicits a highly intensified secondary or anamnestic response.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The two special types of lymphocytes in primary and secondary immune responses
cards.back:
B-lymphocytes
T-lymphocytes
cards.quote: The primary and secondary immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in our blood, i.e., B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are antibodies, and which cells produce them?
cards.back: The B-lymphocytes produce an army of proteins in response to pathogens into our blood to fight with them. These proteins are called antibodies.
cards.quote: The B-lymphocytes produce an army of proteins in response to pathogens into our blood to fight with them. These proteins are called antibodies.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the role of T-cells in antibody production?
cards.back: The T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B cells to produce them.
cards.quote: The T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B cells to produce them.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many peptide chains does an antibody molecule have, and which are they?
cards.back: Each antibody molecule has four peptide chains, two small called light chains and two longer called heavy chains.
cards.quote: Each antibody molecule has four peptide chains, two small called light chains and two longer called heavy chains.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How is an antibody represented (in terms of heavy and light chains)?
cards.back: Hence, an antibody is represented as H2L2.
cards.quote: Hence, an antibody is represented as H2L2.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the types of antibodies given in NCERT.
cards.back:
IgA
IgM
IgE
IgG
cards.quote: Different types of antibodies are produced in our body. IgA, IgM, IgE, IgG are some of them.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the antibody-mediated acquired immune response also called, and why?
cards.back: Because these antibodies are found in the blood, the response is also called as humoral immune response.
cards.quote: Because these antibodies are found in the blood, the response is also called as humoral immune response.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity (CMI)?
cards.back: cell-mediated immune response or cell-mediated immunity (CMI). The T-lymphocytes mediate CMI.
cards.quote: cell-mediated immune response or cell-mediated immunity (CMI). The T-lymphocytes mediate CMI.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which immune response is responsible for graft rejection?
cards.back: the cell-mediated immune response is responsible for the graft rejection.
cards.quote: the cell-mediated immune response is responsible for the graft rejection.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is active immunity?
cards.back: When a host is exposed to antigens, which may be in the form of living or dead microbes or other proteins, antibodies are produced in the host body. This type of immunity is called active immunity.
cards.quote: When a host is exposed to antigens, which may be in the form of living or dead microbes or other proteins, antibodies are produced in the host body. This type of immunity is called active immunity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How quickly does active immunity give its full effective response?
cards.back: Active immunity is slow and takes time to give its full effective response.
cards.quote: Active immunity is slow and takes time to give its full effective response.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What induces active immunity?
cards.back: Injecting the microbes deliberately during immunisation or infectious organisms gaining access into body during natural infection induce active immunity.
cards.quote: Injecting the microbes deliberately during immunisation or infectious organisms gaining access into body during natural infection induce active immunity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is passive immunity?
cards.back: When ready-made antibodies are directly given to protect the body against foreign agents, it is called passive immunity.
cards.quote: When ready-made antibodies are directly given to protect the body against foreign agents, it is called passive immunity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The yellowish fluid ____ secreted by mother during the initial days of lactation has abundant antibodies (IgA) to protect the infant.
cards.back: The yellowish fluid colostrum secreted by mother during the initial days of lactation has abundant antibodies (IgA) to protect the infant.
cards.quote: The yellowish fluid colostrum secreted by mother during the initial days of lactation has abundant antibodies (IgA) to protect the infant.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How does the foetus receive antibodies from its mother (passive immunity)?
cards.back: The foetus also receives some antibodies from their mother, through the placenta during pregnancy.
cards.quote: The foetus also receives some antibodies from their mother, through the placenta during pregnancy.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The principle of immunisation or vaccination is based on the property of ‘____’ of the immune system.
cards.back: The principle of immunisation or vaccination is based on the property of ‘memory’ of the immune system.
cards.quote: The principle of immunisation or vaccination is based on the property of ‘memory’ of the immune system.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is introduced into the body in vaccination?
cards.back: In vaccination, a preparation of antigenic proteins of pathogen or inactivated/weakened pathogen (vaccine) are introduced into the body.
cards.quote: In vaccination, a preparation of antigenic proteins of pathogen or inactivated/weakened pathogen (vaccine) are introduced into the body.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do vaccines generate that recognise the pathogen quickly on subsequent exposure?
cards.back: The vaccines also generate memory — B and T-cells that recognise the pathogen quickly on subsequent exposure and overwhelm the invaders with a massive production of antibodies.
cards.quote: The vaccines also generate memory — B and T-cells that recognise the pathogen quickly on subsequent exposure and overwhelm the invaders with a massive production of antibodies.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Tetanus: what is directly injected when a quick immune response is required?
cards.back: If a person is infected with some deadly microbes to which quick immune response is required as in tetanus, we need to directly inject the preformed antibodies, or antitoxin (a preparation containing antibodies to the toxin).
cards.quote: If a person is infected with some deadly microbes to which quick immune response is required as in tetanus, we need to directly inject the preformed antibodies, or antitoxin (a preparation containing antibodies to the toxin).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The snakebite injection contains preformed antibodies: which type of immunisation is this?
cards.back: Even in cases of snakebites, the injection which is given to the patients, contain preformed antibodies against the snake venom. This type of immunisation is called passive immunisation.
cards.quote: Even in cases of snakebites, the injection which is given to the patients, contain preformed antibodies against the snake venom. This type of immunisation is called passive immunisation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which vaccine, produced from yeast by recombinant DNA technology, is the NCERT example?
cards.back: Vaccines produced using this approach allow large scale production and hence greater availability for immunisation, e.g., hepatitis B vaccine produced from yeast.
cards.quote: Vaccines produced using this approach allow large scale production and hence greater availability for immunisation, e.g., hepatitis B vaccine produced from yeast.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is allergy?
cards.back: The exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens present in the environment is called allergy.
cards.quote: The exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens present in the environment is called allergy.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are allergens, and which type of antibodies are produced to them?
cards.back: The substances to which such an immune response is produced are called allergens. The antibodies produced to these are of IgE type.
cards.quote: The substances to which such an immune response is produced are called allergens. The antibodies produced to these are of IgE type.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name common examples of allergens.
cards.back: Common examples of allergens are mites in dust, pollens, animal dander, etc.
cards.quote: Common examples of allergens are mites in dust, pollens, animal dander, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Allergy: what are the symptoms of allergic reactions?
cards.back: Symptoms of allergic reactions include sneezing, watery eyes, running nose and difficulty in breathing.
cards.quote: Symptoms of allergic reactions include sneezing, watery eyes, running nose and difficulty in breathing.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Allergy is due to the release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from the ____.
cards.back: Allergy is due to the release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from the mast cells.
cards.quote: Allergy is due to the release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from the mast cells.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which drugs quickly reduce the symptoms of allergy?
cards.back: The use of drugs like anti-histamine, adrenalin and steroids quickly reduce the symptoms of allergy.
cards.quote: The use of drugs like anti-histamine, adrenalin and steroids quickly reduce the symptoms of allergy.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is an auto-immune disease? Give the NCERT example.
cards.back: sometimes, due to genetic and other unknown reasons, the body attacks self-cells. This results in damage to the body and is called auto-immune disease. Rheumatoid arthritis which affects many people in our society is an auto-immune disease.
cards.quote: sometimes, due to genetic and other unknown reasons, the body attacks self-cells. This results in damage to the body and is called auto-immune disease. Rheumatoid arthritis which affects many people in our society is an auto-immune disease.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does the human immune system consist of?
cards.back:
lymphoid organs
tissues
cells
soluble molecules like antibodies
cards.quote: The human immune system consists of lymphoid organs, tissues, cells and soluble molecules like antibodies.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In what sense is the immune system unique?
cards.back: immune system is unique in the sense that it recognises foreign antigens, responds to these and remembers them.
cards.quote: immune system is unique in the sense that it recognises foreign antigens, responds to these and remembers them.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are lymphoid organs?
cards.back: These are the organs where origin and/or maturation and proliferation of lymphocytes occur.
cards.quote: These are the organs where origin and/or maturation and proliferation of lymphocytes occur.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Primary lymphoid organs
cards.back:
bone marrow
thymus
cards.quote: The primary lymphoid organs are bone marrow and thymus

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the secondary lymphoid organs.
cards.back:
spleen
lymph nodes
tonsils
Peyer's patches of small intestine
appendix
cards.quote: After maturation the lymphocytes migrate to secondary lymphoid organs like spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do the secondary lymphoid organs provide?
cards.back: The secondary lymphoid organs provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, which then proliferate to become effector cells.
cards.quote: The secondary lymphoid organs provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, which then proliferate to become effector cells.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The ____ is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced.
cards.back: The bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced.
cards.quote: The bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Where is the thymus located?
cards.back: The thymus is a lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone.
cards.quote: The thymus is a lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How does the size of the thymus change with age?
cards.back: The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age and by the time puberty is attained it reduces to a very small size.
cards.quote: The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age and by the time puberty is attained it reduces to a very small size.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does the spleen mainly contain, and how does it act on the blood?
cards.back: It mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes. It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms. Spleen also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.
cards.quote: It mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes. It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms. Spleen also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do lymph nodes serve to trap?
cards.back: Lymph nodes serve to trap the micro-organisms or other antigens, which happen to get into the lymph and tissue fluid.
cards.quote: Lymph nodes serve to trap the micro-organisms or other antigens, which happen to get into the lymph and tissue fluid.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is MALT?
cards.back: There is lymphoid tissue also located within the lining of the major tracts (respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts) called mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT).
cards.quote: There is lymphoid tissue also located within the lining of the major tracts (respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts) called mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: MALT constitutes about how much of the lymphoid tissue in the human body?
cards.back: It constitutes about 50 per cent of the lymphoid tissue in human body.
cards.quote: It constitutes about 50 per cent of the lymphoid tissue in human body.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does AIDS stand for?
cards.back: The word AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome.
cards.quote: The word AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does AIDS stand for, and why is it not a congenital disease?
cards.back: The word AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome. This means deficiency of immune system, acquired during the lifetime of an individual indicating that it is not a congenital disease.
cards.quote: The word AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome. This means deficiency of immune system, acquired during the lifetime of an individual indicating that it is not a congenital disease.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does ‘syndrome’ mean?
cards.back: ‘Syndrome’ means a group of symptoms.
cards.quote: ‘Syndrome’ means a group of symptoms.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In which year was AIDS first reported?
cards.back: AIDS was first reported in 1981
cards.quote: AIDS was first reported in 1981

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: AIDS is caused by which virus, and to which group of viruses does it belong?
cards.back: AIDS is caused by the Human Immuno deficiency Virus (HIV), a member of a group of viruses called retrovirus, which have an envelope enclosing the RNA genome
cards.quote: AIDS is caused by the Human Immuno deficiency Virus (HIV), a member of a group of viruses called retrovirus, which have an envelope enclosing the RNA genome

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the ways in which HIV infection generally spreads.
cards.back:
sexual contact with infected person
transfusion of contaminated blood and blood products
sharing infected needles as in the case of intravenous drug abusers
from infected mother to her child through placenta
cards.quote: Transmission of HIV-infection generally occurs by (a) sexual contact with infected person, (b) by transfusion of contaminated blood and blood products, (c) by sharing infected needles as in the case of intravenous drug abusers and (d) from infected mother to her child through placenta.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Is HIV/AIDS spread by mere touch or physical contact?
cards.back: It is important to note that HIV/AIDS is not spread by mere touch or physical contact; it spreads only through body fluids.
cards.quote: It is important to note that HIV/AIDS is not spread by mere touch or physical contact; it spreads only through body fluids.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the usual time-lag between HIV infection and appearance of AIDS symptoms?
cards.back: There is always a time-lag between the infection and appearance of AIDS symptoms. This period may vary from a few months to many years (usually 5-10 years).
cards.quote: There is always a time-lag between the infection and appearance of AIDS symptoms. This period may vary from a few months to many years (usually 5-10 years).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which enzyme helps the HIV RNA genome form viral DNA inside macrophages?
cards.back: After getting into the body of the person, the virus enters into macrophages where RNA genome of the virus replicates to form viral DNA with the help of the enzyme reverse transcriptase.
cards.quote: After getting into the body of the person, the virus enters into macrophages where RNA genome of the virus replicates to form viral DNA with the help of the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What happens to the viral DNA after it is formed in the infected cell?
cards.back: This viral DNA gets incorporated into host cell's DNA and directs the infected cells to produce virus particles
cards.quote: This viral DNA gets incorporated into host cell's DNA and directs the infected cells to produce virus particles

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The macrophages continue to produce virus and in this way acts like a ____.
cards.back: The macrophages continue to produce virus and in this way acts like a HIV factory.
cards.quote: The macrophages continue to produce virus and in this way acts like a HIV factory.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How does HIV cause a progressive decrease in helper T-lymphocytes?
cards.back: Simultaneously, HIV enters into helper T-lymphocytes (TH), replicates and produce progeny viruses. The progeny viruses released in the blood attack other helper T-lymphocytes. This is repeated leading to a progressive decrease in the number of helper T-lymphocytes in the body of the infected person.
cards.quote: Simultaneously, HIV enters into helper T-lymphocytes (TH), replicates and produce progeny viruses. The progeny viruses released in the blood attack other helper T-lymphocytes. This is repeated leading to a progressive decrease in the number of helper T-lymphocytes in the body of the infected person.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which infections does an AIDS patient suffer from due to fewer helper T lymphocytes?
cards.back: Due to decrease in the number of helper T lymphocytes, the person starts suffering from infections that could have been otherwise overcome such as those due to bacteria especially Mycobacterium, viruses, fungi and even parasites like Toxoplasma.
cards.quote: Due to decrease in the number of helper T lymphocytes, the person starts suffering from infections that could have been otherwise overcome such as those due to bacteria especially Mycobacterium, viruses, fungi and even parasites like Toxoplasma.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: A widely used diagnostic test for AIDS is enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay (____).
cards.back: A widely used diagnostic test for AIDS is enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay (ELISA).
cards.quote: A widely used diagnostic test for AIDS is enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay (ELISA).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How effective is treatment of AIDS with anti-retroviral drugs?
cards.back: Treatment of AIDS with anti-retroviral drugs is only partially effective. They can only prolong the life of the patient but cannot prevent death, which is inevitable.
cards.quote: Treatment of AIDS with anti-retroviral drugs is only partially effective. They can only prolong the life of the patient but cannot prevent death, which is inevitable.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which organisation in our country educates people about AIDS along with NGOs?
cards.back: In our country the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) and other non-governmental organisation (NGOs) are doing a lot to educate people about AIDS.
cards.quote: In our country the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) and other non-governmental organisation (NGOs) are doing a lot to educate people about AIDS.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the steps taken up to prevent the spread of HIV infection.
cards.back:
Making blood (from blood banks) safe from HIV
ensuring the use of only disposable needles and syringes in public and private hospitals and clinics
free distribution of condoms
controlling drug abuse
advocating safe sex
promoting regular check-ups for HIV in susceptible populations
cards.quote: Making blood (from blood banks) safe from HIV, ensuring the use of only disposable needles and syringes in public and private hospitals and clinics, free distribution of condoms, controlling drug abuse, advocating safe sex and promoting regular check-ups for HIV in susceptible populations, are some such steps taken up.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Normal cells show a property called ____ by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth.
cards.back: Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth.
cards.quote: Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are the masses of cells formed by uncontrolled division of cancer cells called?
cards.back: As a result of this, cancerous cells just continue to divide giving rise to masses of cells called tumors.
cards.quote: As a result of this, cancerous cells just continue to divide giving rise to masses of cells called tumors.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Types of tumors
cards.back:
benign
malignant
cards.quote: Tumors are of two types: benign and malignant.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Benign vs malignant tumors: the difference on spread and damage
cards.back: Benign tumors normally remain confined to their original location and do not spread to other parts of the body and cause little damage. The malignant tumors, on the other hand are a mass of proliferating cells called neoplastic or tumor cells. These cells grow very rapidly, invading and damaging the surrounding normal tissues.
cards.quote: Benign tumors normally remain confined to their original location and do not spread to other parts of the body and cause little damage. The malignant tumors, on the other hand are a mass of proliferating cells called neoplastic or tumor cells. These cells grow very rapidly, invading and damaging the surrounding normal tissues.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How do malignant tumor cells starve the normal cells?
cards.back: As these cells actively divide and grow they also starve the normal cells by competing for vital nutrients.
cards.quote: As these cells actively divide and grow they also starve the normal cells by competing for vital nutrients.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define metastasis.
cards.back: Cells sloughed from such tumors reach distant sites through blood, and wherever they get lodged in the body, they start a new tumor there. This property called metastasis is the most feared property of malignant tumors.
cards.quote: Cells sloughed from such tumors reach distant sites through blood, and wherever they get lodged in the body, they start a new tumor there. This property called metastasis is the most feared property of malignant tumors.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are carcinogens?
cards.back: Transformation of normal cells into cancerous neoplastic cells may be induced by physical, chemical or biological agents. These agents are called carcinogens.
cards.quote: Transformation of normal cells into cancerous neoplastic cells may be induced by physical, chemical or biological agents. These agents are called carcinogens.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which radiations cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation?
cards.back: Ionising radiations like X-rays and gamma rays and non-ionizing radiations like UV cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation.
cards.quote: Ionising radiations like X-rays and gamma rays and non-ionizing radiations like UV cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which cancer has a major cause in the chemical carcinogens of tobacco smoke?
cards.back: The chemical carcinogens present in tobacco smoke have been identified as a major cause of lung cancer.
cards.quote: The chemical carcinogens present in tobacco smoke have been identified as a major cause of lung cancer.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are viral oncogenes and cellular oncogenes (proto oncogenes)?
cards.back: Cancer causing viruses called oncogenic viruses have genes called viral oncogenes. Furthermore, several genes called cellular oncogenes (c-onc) or proto oncogenes have been identified in normal cells which, when activated under certain conditions, could lead to oncogenic transformation of the cells.
cards.quote: Cancer causing viruses called oncogenic viruses have genes called viral oncogenes. Furthermore, several genes called cellular oncogenes (c-onc) or proto oncogenes have been identified in normal cells which, when activated under certain conditions, could lead to oncogenic transformation of the cells.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: On what is cancer detection based?
cards.back: Cancer detection is based on biopsy and histopathological studies of the tissue and blood and bone marrow tests for increased cell counts in the case of leukemias.
cards.quote: Cancer detection is based on biopsy and histopathological studies of the tissue and blood and bone marrow tests for increased cell counts in the case of leukemias.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is a biopsy?
cards.back: In biopsy, a piece of the suspected tissue cut into thin sections is stained and examined under microscope (histopathological studies) by a pathologist.
cards.quote: In biopsy, a piece of the suspected tissue cut into thin sections is stained and examined under microscope (histopathological studies) by a pathologist.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which techniques detect cancers of the internal organs?
cards.back: Techniques like radiography (use of X-rays), CT (computed tomography) and MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) are very useful to detect cancers of the internal organs.
cards.quote: Techniques like radiography (use of X-rays), CT (computed tomography) and MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) are very useful to detect cancers of the internal organs.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: CT vs MRI: the difference on what each uses
cards.back: Computed tomography uses X-rays to generate a three-dimensional image of the internals of an object. MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiations to accurately detect pathological and physiological changes in the living tissue.
cards.quote: Computed tomography uses X-rays to generate a three-dimensional image of the internals of an object. MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiations to accurately detect pathological and physiological changes in the living tissue.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which antibodies are used to detect certain cancers?
cards.back: Antibodies against cancer-specific antigens are also used for detection of certain cancers.
cards.quote: Antibodies against cancer-specific antigens are also used for detection of certain cancers.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Common approaches for treatment of cancer
cards.back:
surgery
radiation therapy
immunotherapy
cards.quote: The common approaches for treatment of cancer are surgery, radiation therapy and immunotherapy.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is done in radiotherapy?
cards.back: In radiotherapy, tumor cells are irradiated lethally, taking proper care of the normal tissues surrounding the tumor mass.
cards.quote: In radiotherapy, tumor cells are irradiated lethally, taking proper care of the normal tissues surrounding the tumor mass.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Chemotherapy: what side effects do the majority of drugs have?
cards.back: Several chemotherapeutic drugs are used to kill cancerous cells. Some of these are specific for particular tumors. Majority of drugs have side effects like hair loss, anemia, etc.
cards.quote: Several chemotherapeutic drugs are used to kill cancerous cells. Some of these are specific for particular tumors. Majority of drugs have side effects like hair loss, anemia, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are biological response modifiers, such as α-interferon, used for in cancer?
cards.back: Therefore, the patients are given substances called biological response modifiers such as α-interferon which activates their immune system and helps in destroying the tumor.
cards.quote: Therefore, the patients are given substances called biological response modifiers such as α-interferon which activates their immune system and helps in destroying the tumor.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Types of drugs commonly abused
cards.back:
opioids
cannabinoids
coca alkaloids
cards.quote: The drugs, which are commonly abused are opioids, cannabinoids and coca alkaloids.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are opioids?
cards.back: Opioids are the drugs, which bind to specific opioid receptors present in our central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract.
cards.quote: Opioids are the drugs, which bind to specific opioid receptors present in our central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Heroin (Figure 7.7), commonly called smack is chemically ____ which is a white, odourless, bitter crystalline compound.
cards.back: Heroin (Figure 7.7), commonly called smack is chemically diacetylmorphine which is a white, odourless, bitter crystalline compound.
cards.quote: Heroin (Figure 7.7), commonly called smack is chemically diacetylmorphine which is a white, odourless, bitter crystalline compound.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Morphine is extracted from the latex of which plant?
cards.back: poppy plant Papaver somniferum (Figure 7.8).
cards.quote: poppy plant Papaver somniferum (Figure 7.8).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Heroin: how is it generally taken, and how does it act on body functions?
cards.back: Generally taken by snorting and injection, heroin is a depressant and slows down body functions.
cards.quote: Generally taken by snorting and injection, heroin is a depressant and slows down body functions.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are cannabinoids?
cards.back: Cannabinoids are a group of chemicals (Figure 7.9), which interact with cannabinoid receptors present principally in the brain.
cards.quote: Cannabinoids are a group of chemicals (Figure 7.9), which interact with cannabinoid receptors present principally in the brain.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: From which plant are natural cannabinoids obtained?
cards.back: Natural cannabinoids are obtained from the inflorescences of the plant Cannabis sativa (Figure 7.10).
cards.quote: Natural cannabinoids are obtained from the inflorescences of the plant Cannabis sativa (Figure 7.10).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the products made from the cannabis plant.
cards.back:
marijuana
hashish
charas
ganja
cards.quote: The flower tops, leaves and the resin of cannabis plant are used in various combinations to produce marijuana, hashish, charas and ganja.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Cannabinoids: how are they taken, and which body system do they affect?
cards.back: Generally taken by inhalation and oral ingestion, these are known for their effects on cardiovascular system of the body.
cards.quote: Generally taken by inhalation and oral ingestion, these are known for their effects on cardiovascular system of the body.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: From which plant is cocaine (coca alkaloid) obtained?
cards.back: Coca alkaloid or cocaine is obtained from coca plant Erythroxylum coca, native to South America.
cards.quote: Coca alkaloid or cocaine is obtained from coca plant Erythroxylum coca, native to South America.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Cocaine interferes with the transport of which neurotransmitter?
cards.back: It interferes with the transport of the neuro-transmitter dopamine.
cards.quote: It interferes with the transport of the neuro-transmitter dopamine.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: By what names is cocaine commonly called, and how is it usually taken?
cards.back: Cocaine, commonly called coke or crack is usually snorted.
cards.quote: Cocaine, commonly called coke or crack is usually snorted.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the action of cocaine on the central nervous system, and what does an excessive dose cause?
cards.back: It has a potent stimulating action on central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria and increased energy. Excessive dosage of cocaine causes hallucinations.
cards.quote: It has a potent stimulating action on central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria and increased energy. Excessive dosage of cocaine causes hallucinations.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the well-known plants with hallucinogenic properties.
cards.back:
Atropa belladona
Datura
cards.quote: Other well-known plants with hallucinogenic properties are Atropa belladona and Datura (Figure 7.11).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name drugs normally used as medicines that are often abused.
cards.back:
barbiturates
amphetamines
benzodiazepines
cards.quote: Drugs like barbiturates, amphetamines, benzodiazepines, and other similar drugs, that are normally used as medicines to help patients cope with

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: When does the use of drugs constitute drug abuse?
cards.back: When these are taken for a purpose other than medicinal use or in amounts/frequency that impairs one's physical, physiological or psychological functions, it constitutes drug abuse.
cards.quote: When these are taken for a purpose other than medicinal use or in amounts/frequency that impairs one's physical, physiological or psychological functions, it constitutes drug abuse.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Tobacco contains a large number of chemical substances including ____, an alkaloid.
cards.back: Tobacco contains a large number of chemical substances including nicotine, an alkaloid.
cards.quote: Tobacco contains a large number of chemical substances including nicotine, an alkaloid.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does nicotine do to the adrenal gland, and what is the effect on the body?
cards.back: Nicotine stimulates adrenal gland to release adrenaline and nor-adrenaline into blood circulation, both of which raise blood pressure and increase heart rate.
cards.quote: Nicotine stimulates adrenal gland to release adrenaline and nor-adrenaline into blood circulation, both of which raise blood pressure and increase heart rate.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the diseases associated with smoking.
cards.back: Smoking is associated with increased incidence of cancers of lung, urinary bladder and throat, bronchitis, emphysema, coronary heart disease, gastric ulcer, etc.
cards.quote: Smoking is associated with increased incidence of cancers of lung, urinary bladder and throat, bronchitis, emphysema, coronary heart disease, gastric ulcer, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Tobacco chewing increases the risk of which cancer?
cards.back: Tobacco chewing is associated with increased risk of cancer of the oral cavity.
cards.quote: Tobacco chewing is associated with increased risk of cancer of the oral cavity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How does smoking cause oxygen deficiency in the body?
cards.back: Smoking increases carbon monoxide (CO) content in blood and reduces the concentration of haembound oxygen. This causes oxygen deficiency in the body.
cards.quote: Smoking increases carbon monoxide (CO) content in blood and reduces the concentration of haembound oxygen. This causes oxygen deficiency in the body.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is adolescence?
cards.back: Adolescence means both ‘a period’ and ‘a process’ during which a child becomes mature in terms of his/her attitudes and beliefs for effective participation in society.
cards.quote: Adolescence means both ‘a period’ and ‘a process’ during which a child becomes mature in terms of his/her attitudes and beliefs for effective participation in society.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which age period may be thought of as adolescence?
cards.back: The period between 12-18 years of age may be thought of as adolescence period.
cards.quote: The period between 12-18 years of age may be thought of as adolescence period.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the common causes that motivate youngsters towards drug and alcohol use.
cards.back:
Curiosity
need for adventure and excitement
experimentation
cards.quote: Curiosity, need for adventure and excitement, and experimentation, constitute common causes, which motivate youngsters towards drug and alcohol use.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which other factors are associated with drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents?
cards.back: Other factors that have been seen to be associated with drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents are unstable or unsupportive family structures and peer pressure.
cards.quote: Other factors that have been seen to be associated with drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents are unstable or unsupportive family structures and peer pressure.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is addiction?
cards.back: Addiction is a psychological attachment to certain effects — such as euphoria and a temporary feeling of well-being — associated with drugs and alcohol.
cards.quote: Addiction is a psychological attachment to certain effects — such as euphoria and a temporary feeling of well-being — associated with drugs and alcohol.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What happens to the tolerance level of receptors with repeated use of drugs?
cards.back: With repeated use of drugs, the tolerance level of the receptors present in our body increases. Consequently the receptors respond only to higher doses of drugs or alcohol leading to greater intake and addiction.
cards.quote: With repeated use of drugs, the tolerance level of the receptors present in our body increases. Consequently the receptors respond only to higher doses of drugs or alcohol leading to greater intake and addiction.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is dependence?
cards.back: Dependence is the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome if regular dose of drugs/alcohol is abruptly discontinued.
cards.quote: Dependence is the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome if regular dose of drugs/alcohol is abruptly discontinued.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the symptoms that characterise the withdrawal syndrome.
cards.back:
anxiety
shakiness
nausea
sweating
cards.quote: This is characterised by anxiety, shakiness, nausea and sweating, which may be relieved when use is resumed again.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are the immediate adverse effects of drug and alcohol abuse?
cards.back: The immediate adverse effects of drugs and alcohol abuse are manifested in the form of reckless behaviour, vandalism and violence.
cards.quote: The immediate adverse effects of drugs and alcohol abuse are manifested in the form of reckless behaviour, vandalism and violence.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Excessive doses of drugs may lead to coma and death due to which causes?
cards.back: Excessive doses of drugs may lead to coma and death due to respiratory failure, heart failure or cerebral hemorrhage.
cards.quote: Excessive doses of drugs may lead to coma and death due to respiratory failure, heart failure or cerebral hemorrhage.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse among youth.
cards.back:
drop in academic performance
unexplained absence from school/college
lack of interest in personal hygiene
withdrawal, isolation, depression, fatigue, aggressive and rebellious behaviour
deteriorating relationships with family and friends
loss of interest in hobbies
change in sleeping and eating habits
fluctuations in weight, appetite
cards.quote: The most common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse among youth include drop in academic performance, unexplained absence from school/college, lack of interest in personal hygiene, withdrawal, isolation, depression, fatigue, aggressive and rebellious behaviour, deteriorating relationships with family and friends, loss of interest in hobbies, change in sleeping and eating habits, fluctuations in weight, appetite, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which serious infections are intravenous drug users much more likely to acquire?
cards.back: Those who take drugs intravenously (direct injection into the vein using a needle and syringe), are much more likely to acquire serious infections like AIDS and Hepatitis B.
cards.quote: Those who take drugs intravenously (direct injection into the vein using a needle and syringe), are much more likely to acquire serious infections like AIDS and Hepatitis B.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Chronic use of drugs and alcohol damages which organs?
cards.back: The chronic use of drugs and alcohol damages nervous system and liver (cirrhosis).
cards.quote: The chronic use of drugs and alcohol damages nervous system and liver (cirrhosis).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the drugs sportspersons (mis)use to enhance performance.
cards.back:
narcotic analgesics
anabolic steroids
diuretics
certain hormones
cards.quote: They (mis)use narcotic analgesics, anabolic steroids, diuretics and certain hormones in sports to increase muscle strength and bulk and to promote aggressiveness and as a result increase athletic performance.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which kind of parenting is associated with lowered risk of substance abuse?
cards.back: Parenting that combines with high levels of nurturance and consistent discipline, has been associated with lowered risk of substance (alcohol/drugs/tobacco) abuse.
cards.quote: Parenting that combines with high levels of nurturance and consistent discipline, has been associated with lowered risk of substance (alcohol/drugs/tobacco) abuse.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Prevention of drug abuse (i): what does ‘avoid undue peer pressure’ mean?
cards.back: Every child has his/her own choice and personality, which should be respected and nurtured. A child should not be pushed unduly to perform beyond his/her threshold limits; be it studies, sports or other activities.
cards.quote: Every child has his/her own choice and personality, which should be respected and nurtured. A child should not be pushed unduly to perform beyond his/her threshold limits; be it studies, sports or other activities.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Prevention of drug abuse (ii): what do education and counselling aim at?
cards.back: Educating and counselling him/ her to face problems and stresses, and to accept disappointments and failures as a part of life.
cards.quote: Educating and counselling him/ her to face problems and stresses, and to accept disappointments and failures as a part of life.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the parts of the human male reproductive system.
cards.back:
A pair of testes
Accessory ducts
Glands
External genitalia
cards.quote: It includes a pair of testes alongwith accessory ducts, glands and the external genitalia.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the function of the scrotum?
cards.back: The scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes
cards.quote: The scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Each testis has about ____ compartments called testicular lobules
cards.back: Each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules
cards.quote: Each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled ____ in which sperms are produced.
cards.back: Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced.
cards.quote: Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which two types of cells line the inside of a seminiferous tubule?
cards.back: Male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells
cards.quote: Each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inside by two types of cells called male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do Sertoli cells do?
cards.back: Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.
cards.quote: Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which cells lie in the interstitial spaces outside the seminiferous tubules?
cards.back: Interstitial cells or Leydig cells
cards.quote: The regions outside the seminiferous tubules called interstitial spaces, contain small blood vessels and interstitial cells or Leydig cells

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do Leydig cells synthesise and secrete?
cards.back: Leydig cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens.
cards.quote: Leydig cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the male sex accessory ducts.
cards.back:
Rete testis
Vasa efferentia
Epididymis
Vas deferens
cards.quote: The male sex accessory ducts include rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Through which structure do the seminiferous tubules open into the vasa efferentia?
cards.back: Rete testis
cards.quote: The seminiferous tubules of the testis open into the vasa efferentia through rete testis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which duct forms where the vas deferens receives a duct from the seminal vesicle and opens into the urethra?
cards.back: The epididymis leads to vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder. It receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct
cards.quote: The epididymis leads to vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder. It receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the external opening of the urethra in males called?
cards.back: Urethral meatus
cards.quote: its external opening called urethral meatus.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the penis?
cards.back: The penis is the male external genitalia
cards.quote: The penis is the male external genitalia

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The enlarged end of penis called the ____ is covered by a loose fold of skin called ____.
cards.back: The enlarged end of penis called the glans penis is covered by a loose fold of skin called foreskin.
cards.quote: The enlarged end of penis called the glans penis is covered by a loose fold of skin called foreskin.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the male accessory glands.
cards.back:
Paired seminal vesicles
A prostate
Paired bulbourethral glands
cards.quote: The male accessory glands (Figure 2.1a, b) include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which secretion of the seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands is rich in fructose, calcium and enzymes?
cards.back: The male accessory glands (Figure 2.1a, b) include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. Secretions of these glands constitute the seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.
cards.quote: The male accessory glands (Figure 2.1a, b) include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. Secretions of these glands constitute the seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the extra function of the secretions of the bulbourethral glands?
cards.back: The secretions of bulbourethral glands also helps in the lubrication of the penis.
cards.quote: The secretions of bulbourethral glands also helps in the lubrication of the penis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the parts of the human female reproductive system.
cards.back:
A pair of ovaries
A pair of oviducts
Uterus
Cervix
Vagina
External genitalia
cards.quote: The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries alongwith a pair of oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and the external genitalia

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Ovaries are the ____ that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones
cards.back: Ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones
cards.quote: Ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Into which two zones is the stroma of the ovary divided?
cards.back: Each ovary is covered by a thin epithelium which encloses the ovarian stroma. The stroma is divided into two zones – a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla.
cards.quote: Each ovary is covered by a thin epithelium which encloses the ovarian stroma. The stroma is divided into two zones a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the female accessory ducts.
cards.back:
Oviducts (fallopian tubes)
Uterus
Vagina
cards.quote: The oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called ____
cards.back: The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae
cards.quote: The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which part of the oviduct lies closest to the ovary?
cards.back: The funnel-shaped infundibulum
cards.quote: the part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which part of the oviduct does the infundibulum lead to?
cards.back: part of the oviduct called ampulla.
cards.quote: part of the oviduct called ampulla.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the last part of the oviduct, which joins the uterus, called?
cards.back: The last part of the oviduct, isthmus has a narrow lumen and it joins the uterus.
cards.quote: The last part of the oviduct, isthmus has a narrow lumen and it joins the uterus.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The uterus is single and it is also called ____. The shape of the uterus is like an inverted pear.
