cards.back: The uterus is single and it is also called womb. The shape of the uterus is like an inverted pear.
cards.quote: The uterus is single and it is also called womb. The shape of the uterus is like an inverted pear.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The cervical canal alongwith which structure forms the birth canal?
cards.back: Vagina
cards.quote: which alongwith vagina forms the birth canal.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the three layers of the uterine wall.
cards.back:
The external thin membranous perimetrium
middle thick layer of smooth muscle, myometrium
inner glandular layer called endometrium that lines the uterine cavity.
cards.quote: The external thin membranous perimetrium, middle thick layer of smooth muscle, myometrium and inner glandular layer called endometrium that lines the uterine cavity.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which uterine layer shows cyclical changes in the menstrual cycle and which contracts strongly during delivery?
cards.back: The endometrium undergoes cyclical changes during menstrual cycle while the myometrium exhibits strong contraction during delivery of the baby.
cards.quote: The endometrium undergoes cyclical changes during menstrual cycle while the myometrium exhibits strong contraction during delivery of the baby.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the female external genitalia.
cards.back:
Mons pubis
Labia majora
Labia minora
Hymen
Clitoris
cards.quote: The female external genitalia include mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In fact, the presence or absence of ____ is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience.
cards.back: In fact, the presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience.
cards.quote: In fact, the presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many mammary lobes does the glandular tissue of each breast have, and what do they contain?
cards.back: 15-20 mammary lobes, containing clusters of cells called alveoli
cards.quote: The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do the cells of the alveoli secrete?
cards.back: The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli.
cards.quote: The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Trace the path of milk from the alveoli to the nipple.
cards.back:
Alveoli
Mammary tubules
Mammary duct
Mammary ampulla
Lactiferous duct
Nipple
cards.quote: The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla which is connected to lactiferous duct and opens at the nipple

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define gametogenesis.
cards.back: The primary sex organs the testis in the males and the ovaries in the females produce gametes, i.e, sperms and ovum, respectively, by the process called gametogenesis.
cards.quote: The primary sex organs the testis in the males and the ovaries in the females produce gametes, i.e, sperms and ovum, respectively, by the process called gametogenesis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is spermatogenesis?
cards.back: In testis, the immature male germ cells (spermatogonia) produce sperms by spermatogenesis that begins at puberty.
cards.quote: In testis, the immature male germ cells (spermatogonia) produce sperms by spermatogenesis that begins at puberty.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains ____ chromosomes.
cards.back: Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes.
cards.quote: Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Steps of spermatogenesis from primary spermatocyte to spermatids, in order.
cards.back:
Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis.
A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each.
The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids
cards.quote: Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each. The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is spermiogenesis?
cards.back: The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis.
cards.quote: The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: After spermiogenesis, what happens to the sperm heads?
cards.back: After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells
cards.quote: After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules called?
cards.back: Spermiation
cards.quote: tubules by the process called spermiation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (____).
cards.back: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH).
cards.quote: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: GnRH (gonadotropin releasing hormone) is a hormone of which part of the brain?
cards.back:
Hypothalamus
This, if you recall, is a hypothalamic hormone.
cards.quote: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH). This, if you recall, is a hypothalamic hormone.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which two gonadotropins does GnRH stimulate the anterior pituitary to secrete?
cards.back: Luteinising hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)
cards.quote: The increased levels of GnRH then acts at the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of two gonadotropins luteinising hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: LH acts at the ____ and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens.
cards.back: LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens.
cards.quote: LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens. Androgens, in turn, stimulate the process of ____.
cards.back: LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens. Androgens, in turn, stimulate the process of spermatogenesis.
cards.quote: LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens. Androgens, in turn, stimulate the process of spermatogenesis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which cells of the testis does FSH act on?
cards.back: Sertoli cells
cards.quote: FSH acts on the Sertoli cells

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the parts of a human sperm.
cards.back:
Head
Neck
Middle piece
Tail
cards.quote: It is a microscopic structure composed of a head, neck, a middle piece and a tail

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, ____.
cards.back: The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome.
cards.quote: The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does the acrosome contain?
cards.back: The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum.
cards.quote: The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does the middle piece of a sperm possess and why?
cards.back: Numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of tail.
cards.quote: The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of tail that facilitate sperm motility essential for fertilisation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What constitutes semen?
cards.back: The seminal plasma along with the sperms constitute the semen.
cards.quote: The seminal plasma along with the sperms constitute the semen.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The functions of male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (____).
cards.back: The functions of male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens).
cards.quote: The functions of male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is oogenesis?
cards.back: The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called oogenesis which is markedly different from spermatogenesis.
cards.quote: The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called oogenesis which is markedly different from spermatogenesis.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (____) are formed
cards.back: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed
cards.quote: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Are any more oogonia formed after birth?
cards.back: no more oogonia are formed and added after birth.
cards.quote: no more oogonia are formed and added after birth.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are the cells called that enter prophase-I of meiosis and are temporarily arrested at that stage in the fetal ovary?
cards.back: Primary oocytes
cards.quote: These cells start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage, called primary oocytes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Each primary oocyte then gets surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells and is called the ____
cards.back: Each primary oocyte then gets surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells and is called the primary follicle
cards.quote: Each primary oocyte then gets surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells and is called the primary follicle

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many primary follicles are left in each ovary at puberty?
cards.back:
60,000-80,000
A large number of these follicles degenerate during the phase from birth to puberty. Therefore, at puberty only 60,000-80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary.
cards.quote: A large number of these follicles degenerate during the phase from birth to puberty. Therefore, at puberty only 60,000-80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca and are called ____.
cards.back: The primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca and are called secondary follicles.
cards.quote: The primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca and are called secondary follicles.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called ____.
cards.back: The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called antrum.
cards.quote: The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called antrum.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Into which two layers is the theca organised in a tertiary follicle?
cards.back: The theca layer is organised into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa.
cards.quote: The theca layer is organised into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is formed when the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division in the tertiary follicle?
cards.back: A large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body
cards.quote: It is an unequal division resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ retains bulk of the nutrient rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte.
cards.back: secondary oocyte retains bulk of the nutrient rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte.
cards.quote: secondary oocyte retains bulk of the nutrient rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or ____
cards.back: The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or Graafian follicle
cards.quote: The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or Graafian follicle

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called ____ surrounding it.
cards.back: The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it.
cards.quote: The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is ovulation?
cards.back: The Graafian follicle now ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovum) from the ovary by the process called ovulation.
cards.quote: The Graafian follicle now ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovum) from the ovary by the process called ovulation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define the menstrual cycle.
cards.back: The reproductive cycle in the female primates (e.g. monkeys, apes and human beings) is called menstrual cycle.
cards.quote: The reproductive cycle in the female primates (e.g. monkeys, apes and human beings) is called menstrual cycle.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is menarche?
cards.back: The first menstruation begins at puberty and is called menarche.
cards.quote: The first menstruation begins at puberty and is called menarche.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In human females, menstruation is repeated at an average interval of about ____
cards.back: In human females, menstruation is repeated at an average interval of about 28/29 days
cards.quote: In human females, menstruation is repeated at an average interval of about 28/29 days

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What happens in the menstrual phase and how long does it last?
cards.back: The cycle starts with the menstrual phase, when menstrual flow occurs and it lasts for 3-5 days.
cards.quote: The cycle starts with the menstrual phase, when menstrual flow occurs and it lasts for 3-5 days.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What causes the menstrual flow?
cards.back: The menstrual flow results due to breakdown of endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels which forms liquid that comes out through vagina.
cards.quote: The menstrual flow results due to breakdown of endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels which forms liquid that comes out through vagina.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is ____.
cards.back: Menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised.
cards.quote: Menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What happens in the follicular phase?
cards.back: During this phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium of uterus regenerates through proliferation.
cards.quote: During this phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium of uterus regenerates through proliferation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of cycle (about ____).
cards.back: Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of cycle (about 14th day).
cards.quote: Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of cycle (about 14th day).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the LH surge?
cards.back: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of ovum (ovulation).
cards.quote: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of ovum (ovulation).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What forms during the luteal phase?
cards.back:
The corpus luteum
The ovulation (ovulatory phase) is followed by the luteal phase during which the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform as the corpus luteum
cards.quote: The ovulation (ovulatory phase) is followed by the luteal phase during which the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform as the corpus luteum

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of ____ which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.
cards.back: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.
cards.quote: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What happens to the corpus luteum if fertilisation does not occur?
cards.back: In the absence of fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates. This causes disintegration of the endometrium leading to menstruation, marking a new cycle.
cards.quote: In the absence of fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates. This causes disintegration of the endometrium leading to menstruation, marking a new cycle.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is menopause?
cards.back: In human beings, menstrual cycles ceases around 50 years of age; that is termed as menopause.
cards.quote: In human beings, menstrual cycles ceases around 50 years of age; that is termed as menopause.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The motile sperms swim rapidly, pass through the cervix, enter into the uterus and finally reach the ____ of the fallopian tube
cards.back: The motile sperms swim rapidly, pass through the cervix, enter into the uterus and finally reach the ampullary region of the fallopian tube
cards.quote: The motile sperms swim rapidly, pass through the cervix, enter into the uterus and finally reach the ampullary region of the fallopian tube

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What must occur for fertilisation to take place?
cards.back: Fertilisation can only occur if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region.
cards.quote: Fertilisation can only occur if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is fertilisation?
cards.back: The process of fusion of a sperm with an ovum is called fertilisation.
cards.quote: The process of fusion of a sperm with an ovum is called fertilisation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: With which layer of the ovum does a sperm first come in contact during fertilisation?
cards.back: Zona pellucida
cards.quote: a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: During fertilisation, what blocks the entry of additional sperms into the ovum?
cards.back: During fertilisation, a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum (Figure 2.10) and induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms.
cards.quote: During fertilisation, a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum (Figure 2.10) and induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How does the sperm enter the cytoplasm of the ovum?
cards.back: The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida
cards.quote: The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What results from the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte at fertilisation?
cards.back: A second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid)
cards.quote: The second meiotic division is also unequal and results in the formation of a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Soon the haploid nucleus of the sperms and that of the ovum fuse together to form a ____.
cards.back: Soon the haploid nucleus of the sperms and that of the ovum fuse together to form a diploid zygote.
cards.quote: Soon the haploid nucleus of the sperms and that of the ovum fuse together to form a diploid zygote.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Scientifically, who determines the sex of the baby, the father or the mother?
cards.back: The father
cards.quote: scientifically it is correct to say that the sex of the baby is determined by the father and not by the mother!

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The zygote carrying ____ would develop into a female baby and ____ would form a male
cards.back: The zygote carrying XX would develop into a female baby and XY would form a male
cards.quote: The zygote carrying XX would develop into a female baby and XY would form a male

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is cleavage?
cards.back: The mitotic division starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct called cleavage
cards.quote: The mitotic division starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct called cleavage

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are the 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells formed by cleavage called?
cards.back: Blastomeres
cards.quote: and forms 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells called blastomeres.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres called?
cards.back: Morula
cards.quote: blastomeres is called a morula

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Into which two parts are the blastomeres of the blastocyst arranged?
cards.back: The blastomeres in the blastocyst are arranged into an outer layer called trophoblast and an inner group of cells attached to trophoblast called the inner cell mass.
cards.quote: The blastomeres in the blastocyst are arranged into an outer layer called trophoblast and an inner group of cells attached to trophoblast called the inner cell mass.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does the inner cell mass differentiate into?
cards.back: The trophoblast layer then gets attached to the endometrium and the inner cell mass gets differentiated as the embryo.
cards.quote: The trophoblast layer then gets attached to the endometrium and the inner cell mass gets differentiated as the embryo.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: As a result, the blastocyst becomes embedded in the ____ of the uterus
cards.back: As a result, the blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus
cards.quote: As a result, the blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is implantation?
cards.back: After attachment, the uterine cells divide rapidly and covers the blastocyst. As a result, the blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus (Figure 2.11 step H). This is called implantation and it leads to pregnancy.
cards.quote: After attachment, the uterine cells divide rapidly and covers the blastocyst. As a result, the blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus (Figure 2.11 step H). This is called implantation and it leads to pregnancy.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are chorionic villi?
cards.back: After implantation, finger-like projections appear on the trophoblast called chorionic villi which are surrounded by the uterine tissue and maternal blood.
cards.quote: After implantation, finger-like projections appear on the trophoblast called chorionic villi which are surrounded by the uterine tissue and maternal blood.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the placenta?
cards.back: The chorionic villi and uterine tissue become interdigitated with each other and jointly form a structural and functional unit between developing embryo (foetus) and maternal body called placenta
cards.quote: The chorionic villi and uterine tissue become interdigitated with each other and jointly form a structural and functional unit between developing embryo (foetus) and maternal body called placenta

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are the functions of the placenta?
cards.back: The placenta facilitate the supply of oxygen and nutrients to the embryo and also removal of carbon dioxide and excretory/waste materials produced by the embryo.
cards.quote: The placenta facilitate the supply of oxygen and nutrients to the embryo and also removal of carbon dioxide and excretory/waste materials produced by the embryo.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The placenta is connected to the embryo through an ____ which helps in the transport of substances to and from the embryo.
cards.back: The placenta is connected to the embryo through an umbilical cord which helps in the transport of substances to and from the embryo.
cards.quote: The placenta is connected to the embryo through an umbilical cord which helps in the transport of substances to and from the embryo.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the hormones produced by the placenta.
cards.back:
Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)
Human placental lactogen (hPL)
Estrogens
Progestogens
cards.quote: Placenta also acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, progestogens, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called ____ is also secreted by the ovary.
cards.back: In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called relaxin is also secreted by the ovary.
cards.quote: In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called relaxin is also secreted by the ovary.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which hormones are produced in women only during pregnancy?
cards.back: hCG, hPL and relaxin
cards.quote: hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Immediately after implantation, the inner cell mass differentiates into which two layers?
cards.back: An outer layer called ectoderm and an inner layer called endoderm
cards.quote: into an outer layer called ectoderm and an inner layer called endoderm.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: A ____ soon appears between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
cards.back: A mesoderm soon appears between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
cards.quote: A mesoderm soon appears between the ectoderm and the endoderm.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which cells of the inner cell mass have the potency to give rise to all tissues and organs?
cards.back: Stem cells
cards.quote: the inner cell mass contains certain cells called stem cells which have the potency to give rise to all the tissues and organs.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In human beings, after ____ of pregnancy, the embryo's heart is formed.
cards.back: In human beings, after one month of pregnancy, the embryo's heart is formed.
cards.quote: In human beings, after one month of pregnancy, the embryo's heart is formed.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: By the end of the ____ of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits.
cards.back: By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits.
cards.quote: By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: By the end of ____ (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed
cards.back: By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed
cards.quote: By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the ____.
cards.back: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month.
cards.quote: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: By the end of about ____ (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed.
cards.back: By the end of about 24 weeks (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed.
cards.quote: By the end of about 24 weeks (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the gestation period?
cards.back: The average duration of human pregnancy is about 9 months which is called the gestation period.
cards.quote: The average duration of human pregnancy is about 9 months which is called the gestation period.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is parturition?
cards.back: This process of delivery of the foetus (childbirth) is called parturition.
cards.quote: This process of delivery of the foetus (childbirth) is called parturition.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: By what kind of mechanism is parturition induced?
cards.back: Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism.
cards.quote: Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are the mild uterine contractions induced by signals from the foetus and placenta called?
cards.back: Foetal ejection reflex
cards.quote: The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called foetal ejection reflex.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: From which gland is oxytocin released during parturition?
cards.back: Maternal pituitary
cards.quote: release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions
cards.back: Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions
cards.quote: Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is expelled soon after the infant is delivered?
cards.back: Soon after the infant is delivered, the placenta is also expelled out of the uterus.
cards.quote: Soon after the infant is delivered, the placenta is also expelled out of the uterus.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is lactation?
cards.back: The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and starts producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation.
cards.quote: The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and starts producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is colostrum?
cards.back: The milk produced during the initial few days of lactation is called colostrum which contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new-born babies.
cards.quote: The milk produced during the initial few days of lactation is called colostrum which contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new-born babies.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many sperms does the human male ejaculate during a coitus, and what must a normal fraction show?
cards.back: The human male ejaculates about 200 to 300 million sperms during a coitus of which, for normal fertility, at least 60 per cent sperms must have normal shape and size and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility.
cards.quote: The human male ejaculates about 200 to 300 million sperms during a coitus of which, for normal fertility, at least 60 per cent sperms must have normal shape and size and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many ova are released during ovulation in each menstrual cycle?
cards.back: During ovulation only one ovum is released per menstrual cycle.
cards.quote: During ovulation only one ovum is released per menstrual cycle.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Micro-organisms such as Lactobacillus and others commonly called ____ grow in milk and convert it to curd.
cards.back: Micro-organisms such as Lactobacillus and others commonly called lactic acid bacteria (LAB) grow in milk and convert it to curd.
cards.quote: Micro-organisms such as Lactobacillus and others commonly called lactic acid bacteria (LAB) grow in milk and convert it to curd.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do the LAB do to milk proteins when milk becomes curd?
cards.back: During growth, the LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins.
cards.quote: During growth, the LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which vitamin does curd have more of than milk?
cards.back: improves its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B12
cards.quote: which also improves its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B12

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is a small amount of curd added to fresh milk called?
cards.back: A small amount of curd added to the fresh milk as inoculum or starter contain millions of LAB
cards.quote: A small amount of curd added to the fresh milk as inoculum or starter contain millions of LAB

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The puffed-up appearance of dough is due to the production of ____ gas.
cards.back: The puffed-up appearance of dough is due to the production of CO2 gas.
cards.quote: The puffed-up appearance of dough is due to the production of CO2 gas.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The dough, which is used for making bread, is fermented using baker's yeast (____).
cards.back: The dough, which is used for making bread, is fermented using baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).
cards.quote: The dough, which is used for making bread, is fermented using baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the traditional drink 'Toddy' made from?
cards.back: Toddy, a traditional drink of some parts of southern India is made by fermenting sap from palms.
cards.quote: Toddy, a traditional drink of some parts of southern India is made by fermenting sap from palms.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which bacterium makes the large holes in Swiss cheese?
cards.back: the large holes in Swiss cheese are due to production of a large amount of CO2 by a bacterium named Propionibacterium sharmanii.
cards.quote: the large holes in Swiss cheese are due to production of a large amount of CO2 by a bacterium named Propionibacterium sharmanii.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How is Roquefort cheese ripened?
cards.back: The Roquefort cheese are ripened by growing a specific fungi on them, which gives them a particular flavour.
cards.quote: The Roquefort cheese are ripened by growing a specific fungi on them, which gives them a particular flavour.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Production on an industrial scale, requires growing microbes in very large vessels called ____
cards.back: Production on an industrial scale, requires growing microbes in very large vessels called fermentors
cards.quote: Production on an industrial scale, requires growing microbes in very large vessels called fermentors

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which yeast is commonly called brewer's yeast, and what does it produce?
cards.back: the same yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae used for bread-making and commonly called brewer's yeast, is used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices, to produce ethanol.
cards.quote: the same yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae used for bread-making and commonly called brewer's yeast, is used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices, to produce ethanol.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which of wine, beer, whisky, brandy and rum are produced with distillation, and which without?
cards.back: Wine and beer are produced without distillation whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.
cards.quote: Wine and beer are produced without distillation whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define antibiotics.
cards.back: Antibiotics are chemical substances, which are produced by some microbes and can kill or retard the growth of other (disease-causing) microbes.
cards.quote: Antibiotics are chemical substances, which are produced by some microbes and can kill or retard the growth of other (disease-causing) microbes.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which was the first antibiotic to be discovered?
cards.back: Penicillin was the first antibiotic to be discovered, and it was a chance discovery
cards.quote: Penicillin was the first antibiotic to be discovered, and it was a chance discovery

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who observed a mould stopping Staphylococci growth on a culture plate?
cards.back: Alexander Fleming while working on Staphylococci bacteria, once observed a mould growing in one of his unwashed culture plates around which Staphylococci could not grow.
cards.quote: Alexander Fleming while working on Staphylococci bacteria, once observed a mould growing in one of his unwashed culture plates around which Staphylococci could not grow.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: After which mould did Fleming name Penicillin?
cards.back: he named it Penicillin after the mould Penicillium notatum
cards.quote: he named it Penicillin after the mould Penicillium notatum

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who established the full potential of penicillin as an effective antibiotic?
cards.back: its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established much later by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey.
cards.quote: its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established much later by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the microbe that produces each of citric, acetic, butyric and lactic acid.
cards.back:
Aspergillus niger (a fungus) of citric acid
Acetobacter aceti (a bacterium) of acetic acid
Clostridium butylicum (a bacterium) of butyric acid
Lactobacillus (a bacterium) of lactic acid
cards.quote: Examples of acid producers are Aspergillus niger (a fungus) of citric acid, Acetobacter aceti (a bacterium) of acetic acid; Clostridium butylicum (a bacterium) of butyric acid and Lactobacillus (a bacterium) of lactic acid.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which microbe is used for commercial production of ethanol?
cards.back: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used for commercial production of ethanol.
cards.quote: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used for commercial production of ethanol.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are lipases used for in detergent formulations?
cards.back: Lipases are used in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily stains from the laundry.
cards.quote: Lipases are used in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily stains from the laundry.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which enzymes are used to clarify bottled fruit juices?
cards.back: bottled juices are clarified by the use of pectinases and proteases
cards.quote: bottled juices are clarified by the use of pectinases and proteases

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is streptokinase used for, and which bacterium produces it?
cards.back: Streptokinase produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering is used as a clot buster for removing clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction leading to heart attack.
cards.quote: Streptokinase produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering is used as a clot buster for removing clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction leading to heart attack.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which fungus produces cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive agent?
cards.back: cyclosporin A, that is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.
cards.quote: cyclosporin A, that is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which yeast produces statins, the blood-cholesterol lowering agents?
cards.back: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus have been commercialised as blood-cholesterol lowering agents.
cards.quote: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus have been commercialised as blood-cholesterol lowering agents.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How do statins lower blood cholesterol?
cards.back: It acts by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for synthesis of cholesterol.
cards.quote: It acts by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for synthesis of cholesterol.

source.section: Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is sewage?
cards.back: A major component of this waste water is human excreta. This municipal waste-water is also called sewage.
cards.quote: A major component of this waste water is human excreta. This municipal waste-water is also called sewage.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Sewage is treated in sewage ____ to make it less polluting.
cards.back: Sewage is treated in sewage treatment plants (STPs) to make it less polluting.
cards.quote: Sewage is treated in sewage treatment plants (STPs) to make it less polluting.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which microbes carry out the treatment of waste water in sewage?
cards.back: heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage
cards.quote: heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does primary treatment of sewage involve?
cards.back: These treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles - large and small - from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation.
cards.quote: These treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles - large and small - from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Primary treatment: how debris and grit are removed, in order
cards.back:
floating debris is removed by sequential filtration
the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation
cards.quote: initially, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration. Then the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What do all the solids that settle in primary treatment form?
cards.back: All solids that settle form the primary sludge
cards.quote: All solids that settle form the primary sludge

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Where is primary effluent passed in secondary (biological) treatment?
cards.back: The primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks (Figure 8.6) where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it.
cards.quote: The primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks (Figure 8.6) where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are flocs?
cards.back: flocs (masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh like structures)
cards.quote: flocs (masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh like structures)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define BOD (biochemical oxygen demand).
cards.back: BOD refers to the amount of the oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria.
cards.quote: BOD refers to the amount of the oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does the BOD test measure?
cards.back: The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of oxygen by micro-organisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water.
cards.quote: The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of oxygen by micro-organisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The greater the ____ of waste water, more is its polluting potential.
cards.back: The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential.
cards.quote: The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is activated sludge?
cards.back: the bacterial flocs are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge.
cards.quote: the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial flocs are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is a small part of the activated sludge used for?
cards.back: A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum.
cards.quote: A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In sewage treatment, what are the large tanks called into which the major part of the activated sludge is pumped?
cards.back: The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters.
cards.quote: The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the gases that bacteria produce during anaerobic sludge digestion.
cards.back:
methane
hydrogen sulphide
carbon dioxide
cards.quote: bacteria produce a mixture of gases such as methane, hydrogen sulphide and carbon dioxide

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Where is the effluent from the secondary treatment plant generally released?
cards.back: The effluent from the secondary treatment plant is generally released into natural water bodies like rivers and streams.
cards.quote: The effluent from the secondary treatment plant is generally released into natural water bodies like rivers and streams.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which two action plans did the Ministry of Environment and Forests initiate to save major rivers?
cards.back: The Ministry of Environment and Forests has initiated Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to save these major rivers of our country from pollution.
cards.quote: The Ministry of Environment and Forests has initiated Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to save these major rivers of our country from pollution.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is biogas?
cards.back: Biogas is a mixture of gases (containing predominantly methane) produced by the microbial activity and which may be used as fuel.
cards.quote: Biogas is a mixture of gases (containing predominantly methane) produced by the microbial activity and which may be used as fuel.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are methanogens? Name a common one.
cards.back: certain bacteria, which grow anaerobically on cellulosic material, produce large amount of methane along with CO2 and H2. These bacteria are collectively called methanogens, and one such common bacterium is Methanobacterium.
cards.quote: certain bacteria, which grow anaerobically on cellulosic material, produce large amount of methane along with CO2 and H2. These bacteria are collectively called methanogens, and one such common bacterium is Methanobacterium.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Besides cattle rumen, where are methanogens commonly found?
cards.back: These bacteria are commonly found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment. These bacteria are also present in the rumen (a part of stomach) of cattle.
cards.quote: These bacteria are commonly found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment. These bacteria are also present in the rumen (a part of stomach) of cattle.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Dung can be used for generation of biogas, commonly called ____.
cards.back: Dung can be used for generation of biogas, commonly called gobar gas.
cards.quote: Dung can be used for generation of biogas, commonly called gobar gas.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What does a biogas plant consist of?
cards.back: The biogas plant consists of a concrete tank (10-15 feet deep) in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed.
cards.quote: The biogas plant consists of a concrete tank (10-15 feet deep) in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How may the spent slurry removed from a biogas plant be used?
cards.back: The spent slurry is removed through another outlet and may be used as fertiliser.
cards.quote: The spent slurry is removed through another outlet and may be used as fertiliser.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is biogas used for in rural areas?
cards.back: The biogas thus produced is used for cooking and lighting.
cards.quote: The biogas thus produced is used for cooking and lighting.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which two bodies mainly developed biogas technology in India?
cards.back: The technology of biogas production was developed in India mainly due to the efforts of Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).
cards.quote: The technology of biogas production was developed in India mainly due to the efforts of Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define biocontrol.
cards.back: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests.
cards.quote: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which organisms get rid of aphids and mosquitoes respectively?
cards.back: The very familiar beetle with red and black markings - the Ladybird, and Dragonflies are useful to get rid of aphids and mosquitoes, respectively.
cards.quote: The very familiar beetle with red and black markings - the Ladybird, and Dragonflies are useful to get rid of aphids and mosquitoes, respectively.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which bacterium is a microbial biocontrol agent for butterfly caterpillars?
cards.back: An example of microbial biocontrol agents that can be introduced in order to control butterfly caterpillars is the bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis (often written as Bt ).
cards.quote: An example of microbial biocontrol agents that can be introduced in order to control butterfly caterpillars is the bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis (often written as Bt ).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What happens to Bt toxin in the gut of insect larvae?
cards.back: In the gut of the larvae, the toxin is released and the larvae get killed.
cards.quote: In the gut of the larvae, the toxin is released and the larvae get killed.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What are Bt-cotton plants and why are they resistant to insects?
cards.back: the scientists have introduced B. thuringiensis toxin genes into plants. Such plants are resistant to attack by insect pests. Bt-cotton is one such example
cards.quote: the scientists have introduced B. thuringiensis toxin genes into plants. Such plants are resistant to attack by insect pests. Bt-cotton is one such example

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which fungus is a biocontrol agent for plant disease, common in root ecosystems?
cards.back: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi that are very common in the root ecosystems. They are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens.
cards.quote: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi that are very common in the root ecosystems. They are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Baculoviruses used as biocontrol agents belong mostly to which genus?
cards.back: The majority of baculoviruses used as biological control agents are in the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus.
cards.quote: The majority of baculoviruses used as biological control agents are in the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which organisms are not harmed by baculoviruses used as biocontrol agents?
cards.back: They have been shown to have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even on non-target insects.
cards.quote: They have been shown to have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even on non-target insects.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define biofertilisers.
cards.back: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil.
cards.quote: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the main sources of biofertilisers.
cards.back:
bacteria
fungi
cyanobacteria
cards.quote: The main sources of biofertilisers are bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which bacterium forms root nodules in leguminous plants by symbiosis?
cards.back: the nodules on the roots of leguminous plants formed by the symbiotic association of Rhizobium
cards.quote: the nodules on the roots of leguminous plants formed by the symbiotic association of Rhizobium

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name two free-living bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen in soil.
cards.back: Other bacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil (examples Azospirillum and Azotobacter), thus enriching the nitrogen content of the soil.
cards.quote: Other bacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil (examples Azospirillum and Azotobacter), thus enriching the nitrogen content of the soil.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which genus of fungi forms mycorrhiza with plants?
cards.back: Fungi are also known to form symbiotic associations with plants (mycorrhiza). Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza.
cards.quote: Fungi are also known to form symbiotic associations with plants (mycorrhiza). Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza. The fungal symbiont in these associations absorbs ____ from soil
cards.back: Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza. The fungal symbiont in these associations absorbs phosphorus from soil
cards.quote: Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza. The fungal symbiont in these associations absorbs phosphorus from soil

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the other benefits plants with mycorrhizal associations show.
cards.back:
resistance to root-borne pathogens
tolerance to salinity and drought
an overall increase in plant growth and development
cards.quote: Plants having such associations show other benefits also, such as resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and an overall increase in plant growth and development.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria used as biofertilisers.
cards.back: many of which can fix atmospheric nitrogen, e.g. Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria, etc.
cards.quote: many of which can fix atmospheric nitrogen, e.g. Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria, etc.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which microbes serve as an important biofertiliser in paddy fields?
cards.back: In paddy fields, cyanobacteria serve as an important biofertiliser.
cards.quote: In paddy fields, cyanobacteria serve as an important biofertiliser.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Define DNA.
cards.back: DNA is a long polymer of deoxyribonucleotides.
cards.quote: DNA is a long polymer of deoxyribonucleotides.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the three components of a nucleotide.
cards.back:
a nitrogenous base
a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA)
a phosphate group
cards.quote: A nucleotide has three components – a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Types of nitrogenous bases, with their members.
cards.back:
Purines (Adenine and Guanine)
Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine)
cards.quote: There are two types of nitrogenous bases – Purines (Adenine and Guanine), and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ is present in RNA at the place of Thymine.
cards.back: Uracil is present in RNA at the place of Thymine.
cards.quote: Uracil is present in RNA at the place of Thymine.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: A nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of 1' C pentose sugar through a ____ linkage to form a nucleoside
cards.back: A nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of 1' C pentose sugar through a N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside
cards.quote: A nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of 1' C pentose sugar through a N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which linkage joins a phosphate group to the OH of 5' C of a nucleoside to form a nucleotide?
cards.back: When a phosphate group is linked to OH of 5' C of a nucleoside through phosphoester linkage, a corresponding nucleotide (or deoxynucleotide depending upon the type of sugar present) is formed.
cards.quote: When a phosphate group is linked to OH of 5' C of a nucleoside through phosphoester linkage, a corresponding nucleotide (or deoxynucleotide depending upon the type of sugar present) is formed.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Two nucleotides are linked through 3'-5' ____ linkage to form a dinucleotide.
cards.back: Two nucleotides are linked through 3'-5' phosphodiester linkage to form a dinucleotide.
cards.quote: Two nucleotides are linked through 3'-5' phosphodiester linkage to form a dinucleotide.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In RNA, every nucleotide residue has an additional –OH group present at 2'-position in the ____.
cards.back: In RNA, every nucleotide residue has an additional –OH group present at 2'-position in the ribose.
cards.quote: In RNA, every nucleotide residue has an additional –OH group present at 2'-position in the ribose.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who first identified DNA in the nucleus, when, and what did he name it?
cards.back: DNA as an acidic substance present in nucleus was first identified by Friedrich Meischer in 1869. He named it as 'Nuclein'.
cards.quote: DNA as an acidic substance present in nucleus was first identified by Friedrich Meischer in 1869. He named it as 'Nuclein'.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who proposed the Double Helix model of DNA, and on whose X-ray data?
cards.back: It was only in 1953 that James Watson and Francis Crick, based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin, proposed a very simple but famous Double Helix model for the structure of DNA.
cards.quote: It was only in 1953 that James Watson and Francis Crick, based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin, proposed a very simple but famous Double Helix model for the structure of DNA.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which observation of Erwin Chargaff also underpinned Watson and Crick's double helix model?
cards.back: One of the hallmarks of their proposition was base pairing between the two strands of polynucleotide chains. However, this proposition was also based on the observation of Erwin Chargaff that for a double stranded DNA, the ratios between Adenine and Thymine and Guanine and Cytosine are constant and equals one.
cards.quote: One of the hallmarks of their proposition was base pairing between the two strands of polynucleotide chains. However, this proposition was also based on the observation of Erwin Chargaff that for a double stranded DNA, the ratios between Adenine and Thymine and Guanine and Cytosine are constant and equals one.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Why can the base sequence of one DNA strand predict the other?
cards.back: They are said to be complementary to each other, and therefore if the sequence of bases in one strand is known then the sequence in other strand can be predicted.
cards.quote: They are said to be complementary to each other, and therefore if the sequence of bases in one strand is known then the sequence in other strand can be predicted.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Double helix of DNA: what forms the backbone and where do the bases lie?
cards.back: It is made of two polynucleotide chains, where the backbone is constituted by sugar-phosphate, and the bases project inside.
cards.quote: It is made of two polynucleotide chains, where the backbone is constituted by sugar-phosphate, and the bases project inside.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The two chains have ____ polarity. It means, if one chain has the polarity 5'→3', the other has 3'→5'.
cards.back: The two chains have anti-parallel polarity. It means, if one chain has the polarity 5'→3', the other has 3'→5'.
cards.quote: The two chains have anti-parallel polarity. It means, if one chain has the polarity 5'→3', the other has 3'→5'.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: How many H-bonds join A-T and G-C base pairs in DNA?
cards.back: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine from opposite strand and vice-versa. Similarly, Guanine is bonded with Cytosine with three H-bonds.
cards.quote: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine from opposite strand and vice-versa. Similarly, Guanine is bonded with Cytosine with three H-bonds.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: As a result, always a ____ comes opposite to a pyrimidine.
cards.back: As a result, always a purine comes opposite to a pyrimidine.
cards.quote: As a result, always a purine comes opposite to a pyrimidine.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The two chains are coiled in a ____ fashion.
cards.back: The two chains are coiled in a right-handed fashion.
cards.quote: The two chains are coiled in a right-handed fashion.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What is the pitch of the DNA double helix?
cards.back: The pitch of the helix is 3.4 nm (a nanometre is one billionth of a metre, that is 10-9 m)
cards.quote: The pitch of the helix is 3.4 nm (a nanometre is one billionth of a metre, that is 10-9 m)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The distance between a bp in a helix is approximately ____
cards.back: The distance between a bp in a helix is approximately 0.34 nm
cards.quote: The distance between a bp in a helix is approximately 0.34 nm

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What, in addition to H-bonds, stabilises the DNA double helix?
cards.back: The plane of one base pair stacks over the other in double helix. This, in addition to H-bonds, confers stability of the helical structure
cards.quote: The plane of one base pair stacks over the other in double helix. This, in addition to H-bonds, confers stability of the helical structure

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: State the central dogma (Francis Crick).
cards.back: Francis Crick proposed the Central dogma in molecular biology, which states that the genetic information flows from DNA→RNA→Protein.
cards.quote: Francis Crick proposed the Central dogma in molecular biology, which states that the genetic information flows from DNA→RNA→Protein.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In some viruses, in which direction does genetic information flow?
cards.back: In some viruses the flow of information is in reverse direction, that is, from RNA to DNA.
cards.quote: In some viruses the flow of information is in reverse direction, that is, from RNA to DNA.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: DNA (being negatively charged) is held with some proteins (that have positive charges) in a region termed as '____'.
cards.back: DNA (being negatively charged) is held with some proteins (that have positive charges) in a region termed as 'nucleoid'.
cards.quote: DNA (being negatively charged) is held with some proteins (that have positive charges) in a region termed as 'nucleoid'.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: There is a set of positively charged, basic proteins called ____.
cards.back: There is a set of positively charged, basic proteins called histones.
cards.quote: There is a set of positively charged, basic proteins called histones.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues ____.
cards.back: Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine.
cards.quote: Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Histones are organised to form a unit of eight molecules called ____.
cards.back: Histones are organised to form a unit of eight molecules called histone octamer.
cards.quote: Histones are organised to form a unit of eight molecules called histone octamer.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form a structure called ____
cards.back: The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form a structure called nucleosome
cards.quote: The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form a structure called nucleosome

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: A typical nucleosome contains ____ of DNA helix.
cards.back: A typical nucleosome contains 200 bp of DNA helix.
cards.quote: A typical nucleosome contains 200 bp of DNA helix.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Nucleosomes constitute the repeating unit of a structure in nucleus called ____
cards.back: Nucleosomes constitute the repeating unit of a structure in nucleus called chromatin
cards.quote: Nucleosomes constitute the repeating unit of a structure in nucleus called chromatin

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: The nucleosomes in chromatin are seen as '____' structure when viewed under electron microscope (EM).
cards.back: The nucleosomes in chromatin are seen as 'beads-on-string' structure when viewed under electron microscope (EM).
cards.quote: The nucleosomes in chromatin are seen as 'beads-on-string' structure when viewed under electron microscope (EM).

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Euchromatin vs heterochromatin: packing, staining and transcriptional activity.
cards.back: In a typical nucleus, some region of chromatin are loosely packed (and stains light) and are referred to as euchromatin. The chromatin that is more densely packed and stains dark are called as Heterochromatin. Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active chromatin, whereas heterochromatin is inactive.
cards.quote: In a typical nucleus, some region of chromatin are loosely packed (and stains light) and are referred to as euchromatin. The chromatin that is more densely packed and stains dark are called as Heterochromatin. Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active chromatin, whereas heterochromatin is inactive.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who performed the transformation experiments in 1928, and on which bacterium?
cards.back: In 1928, Frederick Griffith, in a series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae (bacterium responsible for pneumonia), witnessed a miraculous transformation in the bacteria.
cards.quote: In 1928, Frederick Griffith, in a series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae (bacterium responsible for pneumonia), witnessed a miraculous transformation in the bacteria.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Why do S strain colonies look smooth and shiny while R strain colonies are rough?
cards.back: This is because the S strain bacteria have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat, while R strain does not.
cards.quote: This is because the S strain bacteria have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat, while R strain does not.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Griffith: what happens to mice infected with the S strain and the R strain?
cards.back: Mice infected with the S strain (virulent) die from pneumonia infection but mice infected with the R strain do not develop pneumonia.
cards.quote: Mice infected with the S strain (virulent) die from pneumonia infection but mice infected with the R strain do not develop pneumonia.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Griffith: what happened when heat-killed S strain bacteria were injected into mice?
cards.back: He observed that heat-killed S strain bacteria injected into mice did not kill them.
cards.quote: He observed that heat-killed S strain bacteria injected into mice did not kill them.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Griffith: what happened when a mixture of heat-killed S and live R bacteria was injected into mice?
cards.back: When he injected a mixture of heat-killed S and live R bacteria, the mice died. Moreover, he recovered living S bacteria from the dead mice.
cards.quote: When he injected a mixture of heat-killed S and live R bacteria, the mice died. Moreover, he recovered living S bacteria from the dead mice.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: What did Griffith conclude about the R strain bacteria?
cards.back: He concluded that the R strain bacteria had somehow been transformed by the heat-killed S strain bacteria.
cards.quote: He concluded that the R strain bacteria had somehow been transformed by the heat-killed S strain bacteria.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Before the work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, what was the genetic material thought to be?
cards.back: Prior to the work of Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty (1933-44), the genetic material was thought to be a protein.
cards.quote: Prior to the work of Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty (1933-44), the genetic material was thought to be a protein.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty: what alone from S bacteria transformed R bacteria?
cards.back: They discovered that DNA alone from S bacteria caused R bacteria to become transformed.
cards.quote: They discovered that DNA alone from S bacteria caused R bacteria to become transformed.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty: effect of proteases, RNases and DNase on transformation?
cards.back: They also discovered that protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect transformation, so the transforming substance was not a protein or RNA. Digestion with DNase did inhibit transformation, suggesting that the DNA caused the transformation.
cards.quote: They also discovered that protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect transformation, so the transforming substance was not a protein or RNA. Digestion with DNase did inhibit transformation, suggesting that the DNA caused the transformation.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Who gave the unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material, and when?
cards.back: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952). They worked with viruses that infect bacteria called bacteriophages.
cards.quote: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952). They worked with viruses that infect bacteria called bacteriophages.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Hershey and Chase: how were the viruses labelled?
cards.back: They grew some viruses on a medium that contained radioactive phosphorus and some others on medium that contained radioactive sulfur.
cards.quote: They grew some viruses on a medium that contained radioactive phosphorus and some others on medium that contained radioactive sulfur.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Hershey and Chase: why did radioactive phosphorus label only DNA and radioactive sulfur only protein?
cards.back: Viruses grown in the presence of radioactive phosphorus contained radioactive DNA but not radioactive protein because DNA contains phosphorus but protein does not. Similarly, viruses grown on radioactive sulfur contained radioactive protein but not radioactive DNA because DNA does not contain sulfur.
cards.quote: Viruses grown in the presence of radioactive phosphorus contained radioactive DNA but not radioactive protein because DNA contains phosphorus but protein does not. Similarly, viruses grown on radioactive sulfur contained radioactive protein but not radioactive DNA because DNA does not contain sulfur.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Hershey-Chase experiment: steps after labelling, in order.
cards.back:
Radioactive phages were allowed to attach to E. coli bacteria.
the viral coats were removed from the bacteria by agitating them in a blender.
The virus particles were separated from the bacteria by spinning them in a centrifuge.
cards.quote: Radioactive phages were allowed to attach to E. coli bacteria. Then, as the infection proceeded, the viral coats were removed from the bacteria by agitating them in a blender. The virus particles were separated from the bacteria by spinning them in a centrifuge.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Hershey and Chase: which infected bacteria became radioactive, and what did it show?
cards.back: Bacteria which was infected with viruses that had radioactive DNA were radioactive, indicating that DNA was the material that passed from the virus to the bacteria. Bacteria that were infected with viruses that had radioactive proteins were not radioactive.
cards.quote: Bacteria which was infected with viruses that had radioactive DNA were radioactive, indicating that DNA was the material that passed from the virus to the bacteria. Bacteria that were infected with viruses that had radioactive proteins were not radioactive.

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which nucleic acid is the genetic material in some viruses, for example Tobacco Mosaic viruses?
cards.back: However, it subsequently became clear that in some viruses, RNA is the genetic material (for example, Tobacco Mosaic viruses, QB bacteriophage, etc.).
cards.quote: However, it subsequently became clear that in some viruses, RNA is the genetic material (for example, Tobacco Mosaic viruses, QB bacteriophage, etc.).

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Name the four criteria a molecule must fulfil to act as genetic material.
cards.back:
It should be able to generate its replica (Replication).
It should be stable chemically and structurally.
It should provide the scope for slow changes (mutation) that are required for evolution.
It should be able to express itself in the form of 'Mendelian Characters'.
cards.quote: A molecule that can act as a genetic material must fulfill the following criteria: (i) It should be able to generate its replica (Replication). (ii) It should be stable chemically and structurally. (iii) It should provide the scope for slow changes (mutation) that are required for evolution. (iv) It should be able to express itself in the form of 'Mendelian Characters'.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which criterion for genetic material do proteins fail to fulfil?
cards.back: The other molecules in the living system, such as proteins fail to fulfill first criteria itself.
cards.quote: The other molecules in the living system, such as proteins fail to fulfill first criteria itself.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: ____ present at every nucleotide in RNA is a reactive group and makes RNA labile and easily degradable.
cards.back: 2'-OH group present at every nucleotide in RNA is a reactive group and makes RNA labile and easily degradable.
cards.quote: 2'-OH group present at every nucleotide in RNA is a reactive group and makes RNA labile and easily degradable.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Why is DNA a better genetic material than RNA?
cards.back: DNA chemically is less reactive and structurally more stable when compared to RNA. Therefore, among the two nucleic acids, the DNA is a better genetic material.
cards.quote: DNA chemically is less reactive and structurally more stable when compared to RNA. Therefore, among the two nucleic acids, the DNA is a better genetic material.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: In fact, the presence of ____ at the place of uracil also confers additional stability to DNA.
cards.back: In fact, the presence of thymine at the place of uracil also confers additional stability to DNA.
cards.quote: In fact, the presence of thymine at the place of uracil also confers additional stability to DNA.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which of DNA and RNA mutates at a faster rate, and why?
cards.back: Both DNA and RNA are able to mutate. In fact, RNA being unstable, mutate at a faster rate.
cards.quote: Both DNA and RNA are able to mutate. In fact, RNA being unstable, mutate at a faster rate.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which nucleic acid can directly code for protein synthesis?
cards.back: RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, hence can easily express the characters. DNA, however, is dependent on RNA for synthesis of proteins.
cards.quote: RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, hence can easily express the characters. DNA, however, is dependent on RNA for synthesis of proteins.

source.section: 5.2.2 Properties of Genetic Material (DNA versus RNA)

cards.subject: biology
cards.front: Which nucleic acid, being more stable, is preferred for storage of genetic information?
